title: Whatever you do, offer it to Me

verses.sa: यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् । यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥
verses.tr: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, and whatever austerity you practice, offer it to me.
verses.angle: Yat: whatever turns every act into an offering
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks how to turn daily life into worship. Listen for the one word that turns every act into an offering.

body.text: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer, whatever you give, and whatever austerity you practice, offer it to me. Yat means whatever. Krishna lists five acts, from doing to eating to giving, and tells Arjuna to make every one of them an offering to me. When every act is given back to him, Krishna says, you are freed from the bonds of action and its results.

verses.sa: शुभाशुभफलैरेवं मोक्ष्यसे कर्मबन्धनैः । संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा विमुक्तो मामुपैष्यसि ॥
verses.tr: In this way, you will be freed from the bonds of action and its results. Given over to renunciation-yoga, released, you will come to me.
verses.angle: mamam kritva, by making it mine, reveals the secret of surrender
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna to offer every action and its fruits to the divine. Listen to how this offering changes his very being.

body.text: In this way, you will be freed from the bonds of action and its results. Given over to renunciation-yoga, released, you will come to me. The word mamam kritva, by making it mine, means that the secret of this yoga is to surrender your actions to me. This act of surrender is what frees you. Krishna now reveals that this surrender leads to a direct communion with him, where he and the devotee dwell together.

verses.sa: समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः । ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् ॥
verses.tr: I am equal toward all beings. No one is hated by me, and no one is especially dear. But those who worship me with devotion dwell in me, and I dwell in them.
verses.angle: Samah: equality as the divine default
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is telling Arjuna that the divine does not play favorites. Listen for the exact word that makes this claim.

body.text: I am equal toward all beings. No one is hated by me, and no one is especially dear. But those who worship me with devotion dwell in me, and I dwell in them. The word samah means equal, and it reveals the divine stance as impartial. Then Krishna adds that even though he is equal to all, those who worship him with devotion find him dwelling within them. Krishna then widens this to say that even the worst person is counted righteous if they offer undivided devotion.

verses.sa: अपि चेत्सुदुराचारो भजते मामनन्यभाक् । साधुरेव स मन्तव्यः सम्यग्व्यवसितो हि सः ॥
verses.tr: Even if a person of very bad conduct worships Me with undivided devotion, that person must be regarded as righteous, for the resolve is rightly made.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just said he is equal toward all beings, with no one hated or especially dear. Now he adds a startling condition. Listen to how he redefines righteousness.

body.text: Even if a person of very bad conduct worships Me with undivided devotion, that person must be regarded as righteous, for the resolve is rightly made. Krishna calls even a su-durachara, one of very bad conduct, a sadhu, a righteous person. The word that matters is samyak, properly, because the resolve is rightly made. Krishna now promises that devotion brings lasting peace and that his devotee never perishes.

verses.sa: क्षिप्रं भवति धर्मात्मा शश्वच्छान्तिं निगच्छति । कौन्तेय प्रतिजानीहि न मे भक्तः प्रणश्यति ॥
verses.tr: One who is devoted to Me quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. O son of Kunti, declare it boldly: My devotee never perishes.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to make a promise to the world. Listen to the exact words he uses to seal this guarantee.

body.text: One who is devoted to Me quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. O son of Kunti, declare it boldly: My devotee never perishes. Krishna tells Arjuna to declare boldly. The Sanskrit word is pratijanihi, a public promise, and the promise is that the devotee never perishes. Krishna then names exactly who can take this refuge, leaving no one outside its reach.

verses.sa: मां हि पार्थ व्यपाश्रित्य येऽपि स्युः पापयोनयः । स्त्रियो वैश्यास्तथा शूद्रास्तेऽपि यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥
verses.tr: O Partha, even those born in difficult circumstances, and women, merchants, and workers, can reach the highest state by taking refuge in me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The Gita has been speaking of devotion and refuge. Now, listen closely to who exactly Krishna includes in that promise of the highest state.

body.text: O Partha, even those born in difficult circumstances, and women, merchants, and workers, can reach the highest state by taking refuge in me. The verse lists women, merchants, and workers, and those born in difficult circumstances, to show that none of these birth or social categories bar the way. The word vyapashritya, having taken refuge, is the single condition that opens the highest state to all. Krishna then asks what to speak of you, since even the most exalted have reached the same goal.

verses.sa: किं पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः पुण्या भक्ता राजर्षयस्तथा । अनित्यमसुखं लोकमिमं प्राप्य भजस्व माम् ॥
verses.tr: If even pure Brahmins and royal sages devoted to the divine reach the highest state, what to speak of you? So, having come into this impermanent and joyless world, worship Me.
verses.angle: Anityam asukham: the world is impermanent and joyless
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna compares Arjuna to the greatest devotees and rulers, then makes a final invitation. Listen to how he names this world.

body.text: If even pure Brahmins and royal sages devoted to the divine reach the highest state, what to speak of you? So, having come into this impermanent and joyless world, worship Me. Krishna calls this world impermanent and joyless, and tells Arjuna to worship Him while he is in it. Krishna tells Arjuna to fix his mind on Him and bow to Him, promising union in return.

verses.sa: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु । मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ॥
verses.tr: Fix your mind on me. Be devoted to me. Worship me. Bow to me. United with me in this way, and fully oriented toward me, you will come to me.
verses.angle: Four actions, one promise to him
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to direct four different actions toward him, and promises that this will bring Arjuna to him. Listen for how these four actions connect.

body.text: Fix your mind on me. Be devoted to me. Worship me. Bow to me. United with me in this way, and fully oriented toward me, you will come to me. Krishna names four actions: fixing the mind, becoming a devotee, worshipping, and bowing. He then gives one promise that unites all four, showing that the entire path leads to him alone. Krishna opens the next chapter by promising a supreme word spoken for Arjuna's welfare because Arjuna is deeply dear to him.
